content:
St. Thomas Aquinas presents five ways by which the existence of God can be demonstrated from reason alone, without relying on revelation.

The first way is from motion. Whatever is in motion is moved by another. There cannot be an infinite series of movers; therefore there must be a First Unmoved Mover, which all understand to be God.

The second way is from efficient causality. Nothing can be the efficient cause of itself. An infinite regress of causes is impossible; therefore there must be a First Efficient Cause, which is God.

The third way is from contingency. We observe things that come into being and pass away. If everything were contingent, there would have been a time when nothing existed. Therefore there must be a Necessary Being that exists of itself and causes all others.

The fourth way is from degrees of perfection. We find things that are more or less good, true, and noble. These degrees imply a supreme standard of goodness, truth, and being, which is God.

The fifth way is from the governance of the world. Natural bodies act for an end, even though they lack intelligence. This order cannot come from chance; it requires an intelligent Governor, which is God.

These arguments do not prove every attribute of God, but they establish that a supreme Being exists who is the source of all motion, causality, necessity, perfection, and order.
